question: What happens to the pH of a solution when the concentration of H^+ ions increases?
solution:
The correct answer is __**It decreases.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **pH is a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a solution**, determined by the concentration of hydrogen ions (**H⁺**) present in it.
 
• When the concentration of **H⁺ ions increases**, the solution becomes more acidic, resulting in a **decrease in pH**.
 
• The pH scale ranges from **0 to 14**, where a pH of 7 is neutral, **below 7 indicates acidity**, and above 7 indicates alkalinity.
